title: Best Full Stack Web App Developers (2026): How to Hire One
h1: Best Full Stack Web App Developers
description: How to hire a full stack developer to build a web app: what the project should include, how to brief it, price factors and red flags.
intro: A full stack developer builds both sides of a web application: the screens users see and the server, database and logic behind them. It is a good fit for customer portals, booking systems, dashboards and software-as-a-service products. Projects go wrong when the feature list keeps growing, security is an afterthought, or the code and hosting stay with the developer. This guide helps you keep a web app project on track and under your control.

faq.q: What is the difference between a website and a web app?
faq.a: A website mostly shows information. A web app lets users sign in, enter data and do tasks, such as booking, ordering or managing accounts. Web apps need more planning, testing and security.

faq.q: Which technology stack should be used?
faq.a: Let the developer recommend one, but ask why. Common, well-supported frameworks make it easier to find other developers later and to keep the app secure with updates.

faq.q: How do I protect user data?
faq.a: Ask how passwords, personal data and payments are handled, how the app is protected against common attacks, and where data is stored. Check the privacy rules that apply to your users.

faq.q: Should I build everything at once?
faq.a: No. Start with the smallest version that solves the core problem, then add features based on real user feedback.
Full source code in your repository, database access, hosting and domain in your name, environment settings, and documentation on how to deploy and update the app.
